title: On thermalization in random free fermions: Statistical origins and energy-dependent ETH structure
abstract: We study the thermalization in the random free fermion model by a detailed random-matrix analysis. By computing the ensemble average and fluctuations of $\operatorname{Tr}(Aρ(t))$ for a single-particle observable $A$, we derive the thermalization function $g^2(t/τ_λ)$ with $τ_λ= \hbar/(2η\sqrt{N})$, prove its $|t|^{-3}$ asymptotic decay, and show that the variance of the fluctuations vanishes as $O(1/N)$ in the thermodynamic limit.Particle number conservation is also incorporated into the model, by which we further study the energy-shell eigenstate statistics and prove a factorization theorem of the eigenstate statistics. We further show that under a controlled eigenvector-eigenvalue correlation deformation, the diagonal energy-resolved slope and the off-diagonal eigenstate thermalization hypothesis spectral function acquire an energy dependence.Finally, we compute the fluctuations of correlation functions and compare the fluctuation scales with those of a fully chaotic system, revealing quantitative differences rooted in the Gaussian nature of the eigenstates.Our work establishes the random free fermion model as an analytically solvable realization of weak eigenstate thermalization hypothesis type self-averaging, and as a controllable setting in which eigenbasis chaos can be separated from spectral chaos.
summary: This work analyzes thermalization in the random free fermion model using advanced random-matrix techniques. It derives the decay law for observables and proves that the model serves as an analytically solvable testbed for the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis. By comparing results to simpler ensembles, it precisely quantifies how spectral correlations contribute to the system's relaxation dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the statistical origins and energy-dependent structure of thermalization in isolated quantum systems, specifically focusing on the random free fermion model.
main_result: The model is shown to be an analytically solvable realization of weak eigenstate thermalization hypothesis self-averaging, with the leading relaxation dynamics decaying as $|t|^{-3}$ and the variance vanishing as $O(1/N)$.
method: The analysis employs detailed random-matrix theory, utilizing exact Haar measure calculus on the orthogonal group $O(N)$ to compute ensemble averages and fluctuations of single-particle observables.
model_or_system: The system is the random free fermion model, governed by a quadratic Hamiltonian involving a random matrix from the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE). The dynamics are studied via time evolution operators and correlation functions.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the exact Haar measure moments for high accuracy, and it separates the contributions from eigenvector statistics (ETH) and eigenvalue statistics (RMT).
figures_summary: Figures compare the single-particle spectral form factor between the random matrix theory (RMT) and Poissonian ensembles, highlighting the $O(1/N)$ oscillatory signature unique to the RMT.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by calculating the leading average dynamics using Haar calculus, then analyzing the variance and correlation functions, and finally comparing the results against the Poissonian limit to isolate the role of spectral correlations.
why_interesting: It provides a highly controlled, analytically solvable setting to dissect the mechanisms of thermalization, allowing researchers to separate the contributions of eigenbasis chaos (ETH) from spectral chaos, which is crucial for understanding complex quantum dynamics.
